svg.data-asic: Broadcom Qumran2c+ BCM88840 with a Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM
svg.data-oem-alias: DriveNets NCP-40C6CD-S (Network Cloud Packet forwarder, 4x10/25 + 40x100 + 6x400). NOT A UFISPACE CLAIM - no UfiSpace document mentions DriveNets. The mapping is internal analysis: the okf `drivenets-ddc` bundle's 'DriveNets NCF/NCP to white-box hardware map (shipping platforms)' matches the roadmap slide's NCP-40C6CD-S (Q2C+ 6.4T) to this chassis on published silicon and port configuration. Recorded so a search for either name finds this box; no DriveNets figure or artwork is transcribed anywhere in this file.
svg.data-tcam: TCAM option available to meet diverse deployment requirements (datasheet)
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover performance, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with an additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC, Class C timing accuracy; NOS integration is required to activate any of it
svg.data-macsec: MACsec supported on all ports (datasheet key benefits)
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400G QSFP-DD SR/LR/ER/ZR/OpenZR+, up to 600 km (HIG port table, ports 40-45)
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: 100G QSFP28 SR/LR/ER/ZR/OpenZR+, up to 80 km; 40G (HIG port table, ports 0-39)
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR/LR; 10G SFP+ SR/LR, up to 40 km (HIG port table, ports 46-49)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: NOT STATED. The four SFP+ management ports are named '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports' by the datasheet and '4x SFP+ Management' by HIG Figure 4, and the HIG's Port Overview table - the only place that gives reach and supported optics per port - has no row for them at all. 10G SFP+ is the form factor and speed the vendor states; which reaches are qualified in them is recorded as a gap rather than assumed from the SFP28 row above
svg.data-sfp28-sharing: the four SFP28/SFP-DD ports are in-band port share with 100GE port 0 (datasheet)
svg.data-timing-cable: 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS, 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz, shielded RJ45 for ToD, shielded RJ48 for BITS (datasheet Compatible Timing Cable Types)
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS in on SMA, 10MHz in/out on SMB, 1PPS in/out on SMB, ToD in/out on RJ45, BITS in/out on RJ48
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console
svg.data-sfp-plus-management: 4x 10G SFP+ management ports, numbered 0-3 in their own run
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.","kind":"base"},"dc":{"airflow":"front-to-back","bays":{"psu-0":"ufispace/psu-202-dc@1","psu-1":"ufispace/psu-202-dc@1"},"component-attrs":{"fan-808012":{"model":"FAN-808012-HCE"},"psu-202-dc":{"model":"PSU-202-DESR"}},"description":"Dual 2000 W DC supplies (PSU-202-DESR, a two-post screw terminal under a hinged plastic cover, red latch) with the same FAN-808012-HCE exhaust fans. HIG Figure 4's callout says '2x AC or DC PSUs', so this build is orderable, but no held elevation or photograph shows it seated in this chassis - the DC PSU appears only in its own mechanical drawing (Figure 6) and the cabling figures (26-28). Datasheet input -40 to -72 V at 60 A; maximum system consumption 1220 W under 400G MSA optics and 1524 W with OpenZR+, both below the AC build's figures.","kind":"orderable"}},"datasheet":{"title":"UfiSpace S9610-46DX 46-Port 100G/400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet","url":"https://www.ufispace.com/products/telco/aggregation/s9610-46dx-46-port-100-400g-open-aggregation-router"},"description":"UfiSpace S9610-46DX 100G/400G open aggregation router - 2RU white box on Broadcom Qumran2c+ at 7.2 Tbps with an 8 GB deep buffer and a Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM, 40x QSFP28 40/100G in two blocks of five four-high columns, 6x QSFP-DD 100/400G with 400ZR/OpenZR+ in one 3x2 assembly in the middle, 4x SFP28/SFP-DD 1/10/25G that share in-band with 100GE port 0, and a separate quad of 10G SFP+ management ports; a full timing block (GNSS on SMA, 10MHz and 1PPS on SMB, ToD on RJ45 and BITS on RJ48) with a Stratum 3E OCXO and Class C 1588v2, MACsec on all ports; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Each of the fifty-four traffic and management ports carries exactly one lamp - in the printed band above or below its block, in its own blue light-pipe strip, or in the grey band between the SFP+ management rows - and nothing states what any of them means. The lamp-to-port pairing written here is read off the printed legend (the up-arrow's lamp is the upper port's) and is solid; the STATES are not, so every lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","qsfpdd-400g","sfp28","sfp-plus-mgmt","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The two lamps in the out-of-band jack's aperture are drawn BLUE in HIG Figure 8 - not green, as the S9600-56DX's figure draws the same jack - and are modelled, but this guide tables them nowhere. Because the colour differs from the sibling, the sibling's borrowed green-1G/amber-100M vocabulary is NOT carried over here: both lamps are left with a plain on state in the colour the figure draws them, and what they mean is recorded as unknown rather than guessed from a different device.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["oob"],"wanted":"a management-port LED table in a later revision of this guide","what":"mgmt-jack-led-semantics"},{"note":"Same measure, same scope, two values. The datasheet says 22.64 kg (49.91 lb) without FRU; the HIG's Component Physical Information table says 21.89 kg (48.25 lb) for 'Chassis without FRU'. 0.75 kg apart with no qualifier separating them, so it is filed rather than reconciled. chassis.weight-kg carries the datasheet's figure. It is scoped to the two configurations rather than to the disputed field because the manifest has no id for the chassis itself and the bare weight is what both orderable builds share.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ac","dc"],"wanted":"a revision of either document that reconciles the two, or a weighed unit","what":"chassis-weight-disagreement"},{"note":"The datasheet's physical list and HIG Figure 4's callout both name '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports' and the front figure prints them '0 up down 1 2 up down 3', so the ports and their numbering are certain. But the HIG's Port Overview table - the one place that gives form factor, reach and speed per port - lists only 0~39 QSFP28, 40~45 QSFP-DD and 46~49 SFP28/SFP-DD, and has no row for this quad at all. So their reach, their supported optics and what 'management' means for them (a second out-of-band path? a dedicated NOS interface?) are not stated anywhere held, and the group carries the datasheet's media and speed and nothing else.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["sfp-plus-mgmt"],"wanted":"a Port Overview row for the SFP+ management quad, or a NOS integration guide","what":"sfp-plus-management-ports"},{"note":"FAN-808012-HCE appears in this datasheet as an ordering line with no wattage, exactly as it does in the S9321-64E documents the component was built from, and this HIG dimensions and weighs the fan without publishing a draw. The component's own provenance records the searches already run there. The consequence for THIS device is that the sum of the modelled modules' power is a floor and not a total, and the L27 warning on this fan is the record of it.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ufispace/fan-808012@1"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-808012-HCE","what":"fan-power"},{"note":"This HIG gives the fan FRU as 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 mm; the S9321-64E HIG, from which ufispace/fan-808012 was built, gives 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 mm for the same part number - those agree. What does NOT agree is the weight: this guide says 750 g and that one says 741 g. Nine grams, on a part whose geometry both documents state identically, so the component is reused unchanged rather than forked.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-808012@1"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-808012-HCE","what":"fan-dimension-disagreement"},{"note":"No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9610-46DX in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. This says only that we hold no document naming one.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9610 aggregation line","what":"chassis-sku"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - 3+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management block at the left of the faceplate - the RS-232 console RJ45, the micro-USB serial console, the USB 3.0 service port, the out-of-band RJ45 and the recessed reset button. Same block, and the same word for it, as the library's other UfiSpace white boxes","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port - one lamp per QSFP28 port in the printed green bands, one per QSFP-DD port in its blue light-pipe strip, one per SFP28 port in the yellow band, one per SFP+ management port in the grey band, and the two lamps in the out-of-band jack's own aperture","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 hot-swappable"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus-mgmt":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the 2x2 quad below the SFP28 block, the datasheet's '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports' and HIG Figure 4's '4x SFP+ Management' callout. The vendor numbers them 0 to 3 in a run of their own, which collides with QSFP28 ports 0-3, so the ids here are mgmt-sfp-N and rel-pos keeps the printed number","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"description":"the 2x2 SFP28/SFP-DD quad, ports 46-49 of the single 0-49 run the HIG's Port Overview table numbers, in-band port share with 100GE port 0","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the six chassis indicators the HIG's Front Panel LED table names - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and the blue ID beacon","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the timing block down the left edge - a GNSS antenna input on SMA, 10MHz and 1PPS each in/out on SMB, ToD in/out on RJ45 and BITS in/out on RJ48. Five media, one job, and the datasheet groups them under one heading, Timing Interfaces","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9610-46DX","name":"s9610-46dx","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet - Physical, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied; note that this datasheet lists VCCI CISPR 32 and NEBS GR-1089 / GR-63, which the S9600-56DX's does not, and lists WEEE without RoHS, which is also as printed.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2 RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17\" x 30\" x 3.45\"'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple. 436 is the body and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance paragraph states both numbers in one sentence - 'The S9610-46DX width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks' - so the ears are the 46.7 mm difference and are not drawn. Figure 8 corroborates it by drawing two small bracket tabs standing OUTSIDE the full-height body on each side (px 6-13 and 1329-1336 against a body of 14-1328). 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why the datasheet calls it 2RU. The 762 mm depth is the chassis without FRUs; the HIG adds that the fan handles project 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm, which is clearance rather than body.","connector-orientation":"photo/drawing, measured rather than assumed, and it comes out the same way round as the S9600-56DX's - which is stated here because that sibling's provenance warns that the S9311-64D is the OPPOSITE and that nobody should 'fix' one to match the other. A 7x crop of the left block (figure x 310-470, y 30-245) shows each upper module's dotted EMI/latch band BELOW its face and each lower module's ABOVE its face, with a plain white gap between them: the two rows mirror, detail facing the strip. std/qsfp-ganged, std/qsfp-dd and std/sfp-ganged all draw their cage lip near the TOP of the opening, so the UPPER port of every belly-to-belly pair is rotate: 180 and the lower is unrotated. The BITS and ToD jacks were checked the same way at 12x: the upper jack's latch keyway points UP and the lower jack's points DOWN, and std/rj45-ganged draws its keyway at the bottom, so BITS is rotate: 180 and ToD is not. The console and out-of-band jacks both draw pins at the top and keyway at the bottom, so both are unrotated. The USB 3.0 socket is PORTRAIT (its drawn silver shell is 6.6 wide by 13.7 tall) so std/usb-a is rotated 90.","front-grid":"drawing - and unlike the S9600-56DX, whose whole faceplate sits on ONE uniform four-row grid, this panel does NOT. That was checked rather than assumed, because assuming it is exactly the error the sibling's provenance would have invited. The ports sit on two-row assemblies: a column profile at figure x 330-344 reads bright assembly frames at y 47-51 and 131, and again at 141-142 and 224-225, with an eight pixel dark chassis web between them at 133-140. Inside each assembly the two module faces are belly-to-belly about a bright EMI strip whose peak is at y 89.5 and 183.5. Row centres are therefore assembly centre plus or minus 21.5 px: 67.5, 110.5, 162.5 and 205.5 px, i.e. 21.11, 35.18, 52.19 and 66.26 mm. The pitch INSIDE an assembly is 43 px (14.07 mm) and the step ACROSS the web is 52 px (17.01 mm). One grid would have put every lower-half port about 2 mm high.","grounding":"HIG section 8 - the router is grounded through a #6 AWG two-hole lug and M4 screws supplied in the kit, and the guide says 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label' and later 'remove the protective label'. ONE location, not two. UNLIKE THE S9600-56DX, whose figures show that location bare, this rear elevation DOES draw the label: a large plain white rectangle at px 1081-1118 x 22-115 (345.6-358.3 mm, 5.36-37.31 mm) with a captive screw below it and the earth symbol beside it, and the rear product render shows the same white rectangle. So the label is drawn as the metal both images show, and the plate under it is not, because neither image shows it. Earth symbol at x 359.7, y 17.6.","legends":"drawing, positions measured, wording read where it resolves. Readable at 5-12x: 1PPS, 10MHZ, GNSS ANT, the BITS/TOD pair legend with its two arrows, SS for the USB 3.0 socket, RESET, the six system-lamp names, the 0-3 legend under the SFP+ management quad, the per-column port numerals in the green bands and the S9610-46DX wordmark at the bottom right (px 1252-1311 x 251-258, so right-aligned at 430.0 mm). Not readable and taken from HIG Figure 4's callout list instead: the two IOIOI console marks and the two network symbols. The six system lamps' names are the HIG Front Panel LED table's own row order - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - printed dark on a white block at x 4.97-8.95, y 56.61-71.99 with the lamps in a column immediately to its right at 2.56 mm pitch, the same construction the S9600-56DX and S9311-64D use. THE USB SUPERSPEED TRIDENT IS NOT DRAWN: the legend on the metal is 'SS' followed by the trident glyph, and cairosvg rasterises that glyph as an empty box, so only 'SS' is printed and this sentence is the record of what is missing.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9610-46DX end of life' - no announcement found; the vendor's telco aggregation product page for this model and the hardware installation guide are both live, and the distributor listings are current. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.","panel-metal":"THE BRIGHT SHELL AROUND EACH GANGED BLOCK IS PANEL, NOT PART. The datasheet's product render (fig-0003) shows the real thing with the cages EMPTY: dark apertures sitting in a light shell with a white EMI strip across the middle of every two-row assembly. std/ parts draw the opening and stop, so each assembly is drawn here as one light decor rectangle with the apertures placed on it, its extent taken from a bright-pixel connected-component pass over the figure which returned all fourteen assemblies cleanly: six QSFP28 shells per row band at x 100.46/146.21/193.63 and 314.31/359.73/408.14 mm, the QSFP-DD shell at 222.47, the SFP28 shell at 53.05 and the SFP+ management shell at 67.60, the upper band y 14.07-42.21 and the lower 45.16-73.30. A white EMI strip 4.49 mm tall is drawn across each shell's centreline because that is what the product render shows and it is the only bright feature inside the block. Without them the cages sit invisibly on a dark faceplate. The same reasoning puts a gold disc behind each coax jack (std/sma and std/smb draw the bore, not the knurled nut), a silver shell behind the portrait USB 3.0 socket, behind the micro-USB, behind the stacked BITS/ToD housing and behind each of the two single RJ45s, a blue light-pipe strip beside each QSFP-DD cage, and a white rectangle under the six system-lamp legends, which the figure prints dark on a printed white block.","port-leds":"drawing - and the arrangement is ONE LAMP PER PORT everywhere on this face, which is the difference from the S9600-56DX (four-lamp lane clusters on its QSFP28 ports) and is why it was counted rather than carried over. A green-hue pass over the printed bands returns exactly twenty lamps in the lower band, in ten pairs, and the same twenty in the upper band once the light-green numerals are excluded: two lamps per column, at the column centre plus and minus 5.75 px (1.91 mm), the left lamp belonging to the upper port of the pair and the right to the lower, which is what the printed 'up-arrow N lamp lamp N+1 down-arrow' legend says. Band lamp centrelines are 13.50 mm (top band) and 73.46 mm (bottom band), one baseline per band rather than the figure's per-column scatter. QSFP-DD: one lamp in each cage's own blue light-pipe strip, strips at 221.15, 251.65 and 281.32 mm, lamps at 36.00 and 49.80 mm. SFP28: one dark (unlit) lamp per port inside the yellow band at 64.98, 70.13, 82.89 and 88.20 mm. SFP+ management: one green arrow-shaped lamp per port in the grey band between the block's two rows, at 73.28, 76.79, 87.56 and 90.71 mm on y 59.36; those are drawn as plain dots because common/led-dot is the part that fits a 3.5 mm pitch and the arrow shape is recorded here instead - the printed arrows below the block ARE drawn, so the up/down sense is not lost.","port-numbers":"DRAWN, and this is the opposite finding to the S9600-56DX's, so it was checked in the empty-cage render rather than inherited. Figure 8 prints a large numeral on each schematic module face, where a seated transceiver would cover it - that much is the same. But it ALSO prints a small numeral in the coloured band beside each lamp, and the datasheet's product render with the cages empty shows those band numerals still there. So the band numerals are on the metal and are drawn here: per QSFP28 column an up arrow at the column centre minus 8.29 mm, the upper port's numeral at minus 5.47, the lower port's at plus 5.47 and a down arrow at plus 8.29, all measured from a bright-pixel pass over the band that returned the arrows as 7x7 px marks and the numerals as 3x6 px marks on five consecutive columns. The large on-module numerals are not drawn, because on the real panel they are inside the cage.","power":"datasheet 'Typical Power: 626 W (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power sections state the maximum FOUR times, twice per build, and the pairs are different SCOPES rather than a conflict: DC is 1220 W 'under 400G optics MSA standards' and 1524 W 'with OpenZR+ transceivers (on selected ports)'; AC is 1263 W and 1534 W for the same two optic loadings. All four are qualified in a note printed beside them - 'Temperature: 45C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load'. power-max-w carries 1534, which is the highest of the four and therefore what max means; the other three are recorded in this sentence rather than as a disagreement, because they are four measurements of four different loadings. Note that power-envelope therefore describes the TYPICAL figure's scope and not the maximum's, which is fully-configured and says so here. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set: the fans publish no draw at all, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. PSU rating 2000 W per supply from the datasheet's ordering lines; on a single 110 VAC feed the HIG derates each supply to 1000 W.","printed-bands":"ONLY THE TOP OF THE PANEL IS PAINTED, and that was measured rather than carried over from the S9600-56DX, which has a green band above AND below its port blocks. Sampling the figure between the lamps at y 229 and 231 px returns neutral grey (52,52,52 and 55,55,55) all the way across both blocks - the same value as the bare faceplate - so the lower run of arrows, numerals and lamps sits on bare metal and no lower band is drawn. The upper run does sit on paint: at y 38 the strip reads yellow (202,200,78) from px 185 to 298, a grey gap where the circled 'Or' sits, orange (188,119,34) from 316 to 346, and olive green (86,103,69) from 347 to 660 and again from 961 to 1306. Those four runs are the four decor rectangles on this face, and the datasheet's empty-cage product render shows the same four.","psu-build":"THE GUIDE AND THE PHOTOGRAPH AGREE HERE, which is worth saying because on the S9600-56DX they did not. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation and the vendor rear product render (photos/s9610-46dx-3-rear) draw the same face: a vent grid and status lamp at the left, a handle, a large black three-slot AC inlet, and a red cord clip at the right. The HIG's AC section names the mating cable - 'plug the AC power cable (250VAC 15A, IEC60320 C19) into the AC inlet connector' - and a C19 cable mates a C20 inlet, which is what is drawn. The AC build is therefore the base configuration here, and the DC build (PSU-202-DESR, a two-post screw terminal under a hinged plastic cover, HIG Figures 6 and 27) is an orderable configuration that no held elevation or photograph shows in the chassis. Figure 4's callout says '2x AC or DC PSUs', so both are real orderable builds and neither is a gap.","qsfp28-layout":"drawing - forty ports as ten columns of four, five columns per block, and the HIG's own overview figure (Figure 4) labels the two blocks '20 x QSFP28' each, which is the count check. Taking pitch from a feature that repeats once per PORT rather than from the drawn cage bezels: the printed band under the lower block carries twenty lamps in ten clean pairs, giving left-block column centres 346.25, 417.75, 487.75, 558.75 and 629.0 px and right-block centres 991.5, 1063.0, 1132.25, 1204.0 and 1273.25 px. A least-squares fit through each gives a pitch of 70.55 px in BOTH blocks - 23.393 mm - with no residual over 0.6 px. The same centres read off the cage interiors at figure y 55-66 (347.0, 417.5, 488.0, 559.0, 629.0) agree to under a pixel, which is the second independent reading. In millimetres the left block starts at 110.41 and the right at 324.16. The drawn cage interior is 54 px (17.9 mm) and the registry's std/qsfp-ganged aperture is 18.5 mm, so the aperture is centred on each column and the 4.9 mm of bright shell between neighbours is drawn as panel decor - see panel-metal. Numbering is COLUMN-MAJOR within each half-block and is Figure 8's own: the upper assemblies carry 0..9 and 10..19 left to right, the lower 20..29 and 30..39, even on the top row of a pair and odd below it.","qsfpdd-layout":"drawing - ONE 3x2 assembly in the middle of the panel, frame px 685-931 x 89-174, with a blue light-pipe strip standing at the left of each cage. Cage centres read off the cage interiors at figure y 103-125 are 720.5, 811.0 and 900.5 px - 234.29, 264.13 and 293.98 mm, pitch 29.84 mm, which is wide for a QSFP-DD because each cell also carries its light pipe. The drawn cage is 60 px (19.9 mm) against std/qsfp-dd's 19.0, which is the closest agreement between figure and registry anywhere on this face. The assembly's two rows use the same 43 px in-assembly pitch as the QSFP28 pairs, and the assembly centre sits exactly ONE row pitch below the upper QSFP28 assemblies' centre (132 px against 89.5 plus 43), so row 1 of the QSFP-DD block lands on the same centreline as QSFP28 row 2 - 35.18 mm - and row 2 at 49.25 mm. Numbering is Figure 8's: 40/42/44 over 41/43/45, column-major.","rear-layout":"drawing - HIG Figure 7's rear elevation at 2.9106 px/mm. Four fan faces on an 83.83 mm pitch, read THREE independent ways in the one figure and agreeing to under half a pixel: the four green status lamps at px 132.5/376.5/620.5/864.5, the four red 'E' exhaust badges at 126/369.5/613/858.5 and the four red loop handles at 180.5/424/668/912.5 give intervals of 244, 244, 244 / 243.5, 243.5, 245.5 / 243.5, 244, 244.5. The module's own origin comes from the badge rather than the lamp: the badge sits at x 2.2-12.0, y 3.7-11.4 inside ufispace/fan-808012's 81 x 81.5 face and lands the bay at x 10.40, y 3.05, which is within 0.05 mm of the bay a vertically centred 81.5 mm module would occupy. The lamp reads 1.1 mm lower in this figure than the component's own art puts it, and that disagreement is recorded here rather than used, because two of the three features agree. Then a 5 mm chassis strip, the grounding column, and the two PSU bays stacked at x 369.35, 50.5 wide and 40.2 tall, PSU0 over PSU1 on a 42.95 mm pitch measured off their silver frames and centred in the panel. The bay legends PSU0 and PSU1 are chassis silkscreen: which bay is 0 is a position fact and cannot live on an interchangeable FRU.","rj45-pitch":"THE PART IS CHOSEN BY THE PITCH, NOT THE OTHER WAY ROUND. The BITS/ToD pair is one stacked ganged housing, figure px 83-133 x 46-125, so each jack gets 12.92 mm of height. std/rj45 is a 16.0 x 14.0 bezel and cannot sit on that pitch; std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) can, and is what is placed. The console and out-of-band jacks are separate single housings 47 x 39 px (15.6 x 12.8 mm) with nothing above or below them, so those two keep std/rj45.","sfp-blocks":"drawing - there are TWO SFP quads on this face and the datasheet lists them as different things. The upper one, inside the yellow field, is the datasheet's '4 x 10/25G SFP28/SFP-DD ports (In-band port share with 100GE Port 0)' and the HIG's port table row '46 ~ 49 SFP28/SFP-DD'; its cage interiors read px 192-231 and 246-286 at figure y 96-104, centres 65.48 and 83.55 mm, pitch 18.07 mm, on the same two rows as the QSFP28 upper assemblies. The lower one is the datasheet's '4 x 10G SFP+ management ports', which the HIG's port table does not list at all and Figure 4's callout names '4x SFP+ Management'; its cages are drawn EMPTY and dark, px 221-260 and 264-303 by 146-170 and 193-217, centres 75.10 and 89.36 mm on rows 50.72 and 66.13 mm, pitch 14.26 x 15.38 mm. THE VENDOR NUMBERS THAT QUAD 0-3 IN ITS OWN RUN, printed '0 up down 1 2 up down 3' under the block, which collides with QSFP28 ports 0-3; the ids here are mgmt-sfp-0..3 so that two different ports cannot claim one id, and rel-pos keeps the vendor's number. std/sfp-ganged (14.25 mm) is placed on both quads: on the management quad that leaves 0.01 mm between neighbours against a drawn opening of 13.26 mm, and the registry wins for an opening size.","sources":"UfiSpace S9610-46DX datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9610-46dx-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9610-46DX Hardware Installation Guide (s9610-46dx-hig) for the faceplate and rear figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, the port table, the rack attachment-pin count, the space clearances and grounding; three vendor product images (photos/s9610-46dx-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts and construction. Figure quality was gated before anything was measured. HIG Figure 8 (the port overview, fig-0015) measures 1315 x 268 px body - the two small bracket tabs at px 6-13 and 1329-1336 stand outside it and are the ears - against the datasheet's 436 x 87.7 mm, an aspect of 4.907 against a true 4.9715, 1.31% out, so it is orthographic enough to carry geometry and is the front ruler at 3.0161 px/mm across and 3.0559 px/mm down, the two axes taken separately so the 1.31% anisotropy is absorbed rather than ignored. HIG Figure 7 (fan overview, fig-0014) carries the rear elevation above two fan isometrics; its rear body measures 1269 x 260 px, aspect 4.881, 1.8% out, and is the rear ruler at 2.9106 px/mm across; its vertical is the axis carrying the 1.8%, so the rear's y is worked at the same 2.9106 px/mm about a body centred on the drawn 4..263 band rather than at 2.9647, and that choice is what makes the drawn PSU face come out 39.5 mm against the table's 40. HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing (fig-0010) measures 379 x 664 px against 436 x 762 mm - aspect 0.5708 against a true 0.5722, 0.25% out - so unlike the S9600-56DX's equivalent it PASSES the gate and the lid recesses are drawn from it rather than proportioned. The 523 px datasheet front render (fig-0003) is 1.20 px/mm and the 520 px front photograph 1.19 px/mm; both were used for colour, counts, construction and confirmation only.","vent-islands":"derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.","views":"Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing, which prints the fan handles at the top of the panel. This figure PASSES the aspect gate (0.25% out, see sources) so the six long stadium recesses across the lid are measured rather than proportioned: centres 169.3, 268.5, 367.8, 467.1, 566.3 and 665.6 mm from the rear on a 99.3 mm pitch, each 20.1 mm tall and running x 12.7-421.1. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an ESTIMATED position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG's rack mounting section counts - 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins' - plus the M4 screw that locks the inner rail, 'two M4 screws (one on each chassis side)'. The COUNT is the vendor's; every POSITION on both side faces is ESTIMATED, because no held figure dimensions them, and the left face is the mirror depth - x - width of the right rather than a copy of its x. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature.","weight":"SOURCES DISAGREE and both are carried. The datasheet says 'Weight: 22.64kg or 49.91lb (without FRU)'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table says 'Chassis without FRU 48.25 lb (21.89kg)'. Same measure, same scope, two values 0.75 kg apart, so it is filed as a gap rather than averaged. weight-kg carries the datasheet's 22.64 because the datasheet is the spec table and this library takes overall figures from it.","yellow-field":"THE YELLOW IS REAL PAINT AND SO IS THE 'Or' BRACKET, which was checked rather than assumed because a translucent yellow wash over a block is exactly what a guide figure uses for highlighting. The datasheet's product render of the same panel with the cages EMPTY (fig-0003) shows a SOLID yellow field filling the SFP28 block behind its four apertures, a yellow band above it carrying the 46-49 legend, a short ORANGE band immediately right of it over QSFP28 port 0's column, and a yellow bracket with a circled 'Or' running between the two. Both figures show all four, so all four are drawn: yellow field x 56.70-93.16, y 14.40-41.89; yellow band x 56.70-94.16 and orange band x 100.13-110.41, both y 10.14-14.40; the bracket as two silkscreen paths and the word 'Or' at 97.5. circle.data-description: S9321-64E HIG Fan FRU LED table - Off (BMC is not up), Green (Fan FRU function normal), Amber (Fan FRU is abnormal, the fan speed is under 4500rpm)

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)

circle.data-states: off ok critical standby input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output ON and OK), Red (a critical event causing a shutdown - failure, overcurrent, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure or over temperature), Blinking Green (standby state, input power present and only +5VSB on; the firmware-updating boot-loader row is visually identical and shares this state), Blinking Red (input cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply in parallel still fed), Blinking between Green and Red (warning events where the supply keeps operating - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)
